name: Byzantine Court Crisis, Zoe and Michael V
summary: The deposition of Empress Zoe and her successive husbands creates chronic political instability at Constantinople. Michael V's attempt to exile Zoe (1042) provokes a popular uprising; Constantine IX Monomachos (1042-1055) dissipates military funds on court luxury; the death of the last Macedonian empress (Theodora, 1056) opens a power struggle between the civil and military aristocracies that ends with Isaac I Komnenos seizing the throne by force in 1057.

_quarry.structural_significance: The 1042-1057 crisis accelerates the systematic neglect of the Byzantine military, themes are allowed to decay, mercenaries replace provincial levies, and the tagmata are underfunded; this military degradation directly causes the catastrophe at Manzikert (1071); the Komnenos coup marks the transition from the Macedonian civilian bureaucracy to military aristocratic rule
